result:
Round 294 passes: all 9 of my rows pass and every browser row that can run here ran, so `browserVerified` and `realVerified` are both true. One row, B-DESK-SAME, passes only on a substitute check, explained in point 1 below. This round A changed only two test files and one doc; no app source changed.

**What I checked myself:**
- **Claims and scope:** the claims script on A's tree differs only in the lines the task allows. `git status` shows exactly the 10 expected paths. The frozen-file hash check fails only on the 3 granted paths, and the 7 protected files are unchanged. Both test edits match B's sketches exactly.
- **Typecheck and tests:** typecheck passes. The 6 covering test files (90 tests) pass. The slowest test (NG5) used 691 ms of its 15 s timeout.
- **Mutants:** on a scratch copy in `/tmp`, adding the theme marker to the Footer turns ST6 red, and so does restoring the old test map. The scratch copy restored with no differences.
- **B-MARKER (real Chromium):** `/studio-lab` at 1440×900 and 1280×720 has exactly one theme marker, on the workspace root. At 390×844 it has one, on the narrow screen. `/` and `/store` have 0 markers, both in the page and in the server-sent HTML.
- **G294-AUTH (fresh context, no credentials):** the demo page opens with no signed-in user. `/studio/middle-east` shows "Sign in required" with no audio loaded. The studio-token API returns 401 to an anonymous GET and no token to GET or POST, so premium auth is not bypassed.
- **DOC-218:** line 4 is byte-exact, line 21 names both stop calls, the GATE293-T1 entry is there, and every cited id exists.

**Things that deviate from the task text:**
1. **B-DESK-SAME did not meet its literal criterion.** Against the stored round-291 baseline, my screenshots differ by 15 px at 1280×720 and 22 px at 1440×900. Every differing pixel is off by 1 on one colour channel, on rounded corners, and the result was the same on all 3 attempts.
   - I then served HEAD `88b23dd` (the tree that made the baseline) on this same machine. It shows the same 15/22 px against the baseline, while the current tree matches it at 0 px.
   - So the drift comes from this machine's rendering, not from the round. I passed the row on that same-machine check and wrote the literal numbers into the JSON. I suggest B redefine this row as "0 px against HEAD in the same job" (`INFO-C294-DESK-BASELINE-DRIFT`).
2. **`/` and `/store` have no `<main>` element**, at HEAD as well. The row's "no main landmark means BLOCKED" clause can't be the test there, so I judged rendering by status 200 and a visible h1. The missing landmark is an existing accessibility gap for B to rule on (`INFO-C294-STORE-NO-MAIN-LANDMARK`).
3. **No audio, export or timing was measured this round.** The round-292 and round-293 rows were carried, not re-run, and are kept out of `passed`. That rests on the app source being byte-identical to what passed in round 293. One playback check I tried read silence (RMS 0); I dropped it as unexplained rather than counting it as evidence.

**For B:**
- **`A-R294-REVIEW-L-DOC-FILELIST` (Low):** doc 218's changed-files list omits `store-theme-tokens.test.ts`. A's reviewer found it, and it is outside A's grant, so B needs to schedule it.
- **`INFO-C294-TOKEN-POST-405-STACK` (existing, not this round's code):** a POST to the token API on the dev server returns a 405 error page that includes a stack trace (no token). I did not check whether the production build hides it.
- **`INFO-C294-AUTH-ATTEMPT1`:** the first auth attempt hit a navigation race and was replaced once.
- **`INFO-C294-STORE-BACKENDLESS`:** `/store` shows only its hero because there is no backend in the cloud; this is expected.

Ableton conformity is not applicable to a test- and doc-only fix-up. The full suite, build and smoke run are still root's gate rows. I made no app edits, commits or pushes. The second server I started is stopped, and the main server still answers 200.

Files are in `tmp/studio-real-loop/`:
- `c-round-294.md`
- `c-round-294.json`
- `c-round-294/` (evidence folder)
